_comment: Hand-authored mapping: surviving source object -> exact bibliographic object. The matcher proposes; this file decides. Rows are added batch by batch as the author rules them. 'unresolved' names a bibliographic detail still owed - a correct author/work pair is NOT a specific bibliographic object, and the emitter requires the latter.

rows.source: Zhuangzi, butterfly dream
rows.object: Zhuangzi. Translated by Herbert A. Giles.
rows.evidence: Register VERIFIED EXACT with translator Giles; the printed English carries Giles's phrasing ('unconscious of my individuality as a man', 'the transition is called Metempsychosis'), none of which is Watson's.
rows.supersedes: Zhuangzi. *The Complete Works of Chuang Tzu.* Translated by Burton Watson. Columbia University Press, 1968.
rows.unresolved: Exact Giles edition: 1889, the revised 1926 Kelly & Walsh, or the 1961 Allen & Unwin issue. Name the one the text was taken from. Giles d. 1935, so public domain either way.

rows.source: Rilke, 'May what I do flow from me like a river'
rows.object: Rilke, Rainer Maria. *Rilke's Book of Hours: Love Poems to God.* Translated by Anita Barrows and Joanna Macy.
rows.evidence: Register: translator claim correct - the rights-relevant object is the Barrows-Macy English.
rows.unresolved: WHICH EDITION THE MANUSCRIPT ACTUALLY USED. Do not prefer the 1996 first printing automatically; if the text was sourced from the 2005 anniversary edition, 2005 is the legitimate citation.

rows.source: Wendell Berry, 'our real work'
rows.object: Berry, Wendell. "Poetry and Marriage: The Use of Old Forms." In *Standing by Words: Essays.* North Point Press, 1983.
rows.evidence: Work correct at book level; essay identified and prose status established at the source-closure pass. The circulating verse form is a later versification.
rows.unresolved: Wording check against the 1983 edition: the manuscript reads 'begun our real journey', the versified form reads 'come to'. Leave 'begun' untouched until inspected.

rows.source: The Buddha, Kalama Sutta
rows.object: The Buddha. *Kesamutti (Kalama) Sutta*, Anguttara Nikaya 3.65. Translated by Bhikkhu Sujato. SuttaCentral.
rows.evidence: Applied at source closure; Sujato's Nikaya translations carry a CC0 dedication.
rows.supersedes: Buddha. *Kalama Sutta.* Anguttara Nikaya, translated by Thanissaro Bhikkhu. Access to Insight, 1994.
also_drop: Buddha. *Udana.* Translated by John Ireland. Buddhist Publication Society, 1990.
Buddha. *The Dhammapada.* Translated by Eknath Easwaran. Nilgiri Press, 1985.
rows.drop_reason: Both belonged to removed fake-Buddha quotations.

rows.source: Joseph Campbell, 'The privilege of a lifetime is being who you are.'
rows.object: Campbell, Joseph. *A Joseph Campbell Companion: Reflections on the Art of Living.* Edited by Diane K. Osbon.
rows.evidence: Attested to the Companion, drawn from the 1984 Esalen workshop Osbon attended.
rows.unresolved: PRINTING NOT GUESSED: the existing entry says HarperCollins 1991, secondary sources give HarperPerennial 1995. Resolve before emission.
also_drop: Campbell, Joseph. *The Hero with a Thousand Faces.* Princeton University Press, 1949.
Campbell, Joseph. *The Power of Myth.* Anchor, 1991.
rows.drop_reason: No surviving Campbell source object uses either; confirm at the reverse check.

rows.source: Alan Watts, 'plunge into it, move with it, and join the dance'
rows.object: Watts, Alan. *The Wisdom of Insecurity: A Message for an Age of Anxiety.* Vintage Books, 1951.
rows.evidence: Register VERIFIED EXACT, ch. 3; bibliography relationship CORRECT.
rows.merge: The same book is listed twice, with and without its subtitle. One canonical entry.

rows.source: C. G. Jung, 'only a circumambulation of the self'
rows.object: Jung, C. G. *Memories, Dreams, Reflections.* Edited by Aniela Jaffe. Translated by Richard and Clara Winston. Vintage Books, 1961.
rows.evidence: The audit's MISSING verdict is CLOSED as a chapter-scoping error - the entry existed under Introduction while the quotation sits in Ch2. The real defect is the absent translator, the fifth mediated-translation instance.
rows.hold: Do NOT drop 'Modern Man in Search of a Soul' or 'The Red Book' yet. Later surviving Jung objects must reconcile first; drop only if the complete reverse check proves them orphaned.

rows.source: Iain McGilchrist, 'The right hemisphere sees things whole'
rows.object: McGilchrist, Iain. *The Master and His Emissary: The Divided Brain and the Making of the Western World.* Yale University Press, 2009, pp. 27-28.
rows.evidence: VERIFIED EXACT with the page range supplied by the author at 4A.

rows.source: Vladimir Nabokov, 'The spiral is a spiritualized circle'
rows.object: Nabokov, Vladimir. *Speak, Memory: An Autobiography Revisited.* G. P. Putnam's Sons, 1966.
rows.evidence: VERIFIED EXACT; autobiography, not fiction - the census's own corrected suspicion.

rows.source: Rabindranath Tagore, 'the essential unity of the world'
rows.object: Tagore, Rabindranath. *Sadhana: The Realisation of Life.* Macmillan, 1913, p. 109.
rows.evidence: VERIFIED EXACT, public domain, and NO mediation layer - Tagore wrote Sadhana in English himself, which closes the standing 'check, do not assume' flag on his English.
also_drop: Tagore, Rabindranath. *The Home and the World.* Macmillan, 1919.

rows.source: C. Michael Smith, wholeness-making definition
rows.object: Smith, C. Michael. *Jung and Shamanism in Dialogue: Retrieving the Soul / Retrieving the Sacred.* Paulist Press, 1997. - PROVISIONAL, see unresolved
rows.evidence: Register UNVERIFIED with leads open to cmichaelsmith.com and Jung and Shamanism in Dialogue. The live bibliography relationship is not in doubt; the work carrying the vocabulary is.
rows.unresolved: DO NOT assign the wholeness-making / Daimon / Dream Maker / inner axis mundi vocabulary to that work until Smith confirms it. Psychotherapy and the Sacred (1995) is the other candidate.
rows.merge: Two entries exist for one book, with and without the subtitle. One canonical entry.

rows.source: Peter Gabriel, 'One dot, that's on or off'
rows.object: Gabriel, Peter. "Growing Up." *Up.* Real World Records, 2002.
rows.evidence: VERIFIED EXACT; bibliography relationship CORRECT.
also_drop: Gabriel, Peter. "Signal to Noise." *Up.* Real World Records, 2002.
rows.drop_reason: Two Gabriel tracks survive - 'Growing Up' here and 'Darkness' in Ch6. 'Signal to Noise' disappears unless a later surviving object claims it; confirm at the reverse check.

rows.source: Thoreau, 'The fire is the main comfort of the camp'
rows.object: Thoreau, Henry David. "Chesuncook." In *The Maine Woods.* Ticknor and Fields, 1864, p. 38.
rows.evidence: Register names work and page; the existing entry says Walden. Confirmed wrong-book flag.
rows.supersedes: Thoreau, Henry David. *Walden; Or, Life in the Woods.* Ticknor and Fields, 1854.

rows.source: Plutarch, 'not a vessel to be filled, but wood that needs kindling'
rows.object: Plutarch. "On Listening to Lectures." In *Moralia.* - translation not yet named
rows.evidence: Work identified. The restored English follows the sense of the standard renderings but names no translator; the existing entry is a bare 'Plutarch. Moralia.' with neither translator nor edition.
rows.unresolved: IDENTIFY THE TRANSLATION FROM THE PRINTED WORDING. The sequence is printed wording -> identify the closest or exact translation -> cite that translation -> THEN assess its rights. Rights must NOT decide which translation we claim the manuscript uses: 'Babbitt is easier legally' is not evidence. If neither Waterfield (Penguin 1992) nor the Loeb Babbitt (1927) matches what is printed, adopting a named translation becomes a conscious textual replacement in the manuscript, not bibliography cleanup.

rows.source: the proverb, 'good servants but bad masters'
rows.relationship: carried as a proverb with no claimed speaker
rows.evidence: Aesop attribution removed at 4C. Recorded explicitly so the absence does not read as debt.

rows.source: Mother Teresa, 'To keep a lamp burning'
rows.relationship: quotation, evolved wording with a real ancestor
rows.object: Teresa, Mother. *No Greater Love.* New World Library, 1997.
rows.evidence: The repaired byline reads 'after Mother Teresa, No Greater Love'; the audit located the lamp-and-oil image in that book.
also_drop: Teresa, Mother. *A Simple Path.* Ballantine Books, 1995.
rows.drop_reason: A DIFFERENT BOOK, not an edition slip. A correct author does not make a wrong work correct. Drop unless another surviving relationship requires it.
rows.note: The entry became visible only because 4C repaired the byline to name its source - the repair produced the evidence that exposed the wrong entry.

rows.source: Magritte, 'Everything that is visible hides something that is invisible'
rows.object: Magritte, René. (As cited in collected interviews and writings.)
rows.evidence: UNVERIFIED; the census ruled this hedge the appropriate form when no specific source is found.
rows.note: The hedge IS the decision. It is the only entry in the book that admits its own limit, and it survives emission unchanged.

rows.source: Thomas Berry, 'a communion of subjects, not a collection of objects'
rows.object: Berry, Thomas. - work not yet fixed to a verified textual witness
rows.evidence: VERIFIED EXACT as a formulation; Berry states it repeatedly across The Dream of the Earth, The Universe Story and The Great Work.
rows.unresolved: EXACT TEXTUAL WITNESS, not an author-level choice. Do not select The Great Work merely because the formulation appears there and that entry already exists; point at a witness actually verified, ideally the one this manuscript's wording was taken from if recoverable. Identity settled, formulation verified, bibliographic object owed.
rows.note: The second Berry. The matcher offers Wendell's entry for Thomas and Thomas's for Wendell - no string rule fixes this, which is why the pass is hand-authored.

rows.source: Bear Heart, 'Both the sweat lodge and the tipi are round'
rows.object: Bear Heart. *The Wind Is My Mother: The Life and Teachings of a Native American Shaman.* Berkley Books, 1996.
rows.evidence: VERIFIED EXACT; the byline names the work in-text.

rows.source: Goethe, 'The greater the light, the deeper the shadow'
rows.object: Goethe, Johann Wolfgang von. *Gotz von Berlichingen.* 1773.
rows.evidence: Original Act I: 'Wo viel Licht ist, ist starker Schatten'. No Goethe entry exists at all.
rows.note: PRESERVE THE EVOLVED-ENGLISH STATUS rather than inventing a translator. Documented renderings differ from the manuscript's wording, which is exactly why 4I ruled REFRAME rather than CORRECT.

rows.source: Eckhart Tolle, 'As long as the ego runs your life'
rows.object: Tolle, Eckhart. *A New Earth: Awakening to Your Life's Purpose.* Plume, 2006.
rows.evidence: VERIFIED EXACT, confirmed on Tolle's own official channels. The entry already existed; the flag 'Ch5 carries no Tolle entry' was chapter scoping - the SECOND false MISSING produced by the chapter-grouped bibliography, after Jung.
rows.hold: Do NOT drop 'The Power of Now' yet. Held until the complete reverse check. The bibliography is being built from the whole book precisely so that chapter-local decisions are not made prematurely.

rows.source: Shakespeare, 'Out of this nettle, danger, we pluck this flower, safety'
rows.object: Shakespeare, William. *Henry IV, Part 1*, II.iii.
rows.evidence: Register names play and scene. Hotspur speaks it, justifying the rebellion that kills him.
rows.hold: The three listed plays - Hamlet, Henry IV Part 2, As You Like It - do NOT support this active quotation, but another surviving or historical Shakespeare relationship may still account for Hamlet. Held until the complete reverse check. The bibliography is being built from the whole book precisely so that chapter-local decisions are not made prematurely.
rows.note: The inverse of a missing entry, and worse: three entries, none correct. A missing entry announces itself; this one looks complete and sends the reader to the wrong play.

rows.source: Blake, 'If the fool would persist in his folly he would become wise'
rows.object: Blake, William. *The Marriage of Heaven and Hell.* c.1790.
rows.evidence: VERIFIED VARIANT; the byline names 'Blake's Proverbs of Hell' since the 4I reframe. The flag 'Blake present for a different work' referred to the doors-of-perception quotation - both surviving Blake objects come from THIS SAME BOOK, so one entry legitimately serves both.
rows.note: The family that was asymmetric at 4I now shares one honest entry.

rows.source: C. G. Jung, 'Your vision will become clear only when you can look into your own heart'
rows.object: Jung, C. G. *Letters, Vol. 1: 1906-1950.* Princeton University Press, 1973, p. 33 - letter to Fanny Bowditch.
rows.evidence: Register names letter, volume, publisher and page. No entry for the Letters exists.
rows.hold: This Jung object uses none of the listed Jung works, so after two of three Jung objects 'The Red Book' and 'Modern Man in Search of a Soul' remain unclaimed. Keep both unresolved until the final Jung object is mapped.

rows.source: Leonardo da Vinci, 'The desire to know is natural to good men'
rows.object: Leonardo da Vinci. *Codex Atlanticus.*
rows.evidence: VERIFIED VARIANT, closed by an EDITION CHECK against Museo Galileo's Leonardo project rather than by general search. No da Vinci entry exists.
rows.note: Treat the English explicitly as a conventional or evolved rendering rather than pretending to know a translator - the same shape as Goethe.

rows.source: Rumi, 'The wound is the place where the Light enters you'
rows.object: Rumi. *The Essential Rumi.* Translated by Coleman Barks.
rows.evidence: Mathnawi I.3150-3175, rendered by Barks. The book's specimen of honest labelling - the manuscript's own byline is already correct.
rows.merge: Duplicate entries exist, HarperCollins 1995 and HarperOne 1995 for one book. Merge, retaining the edition and imprint actually used.

rows.source: Simone Weil, 'Love is not consolation, it is light'
rows.object: Weil, Simone. - work not identified
rows.evidence: VERIFIED VARIANT, but the register records NO work. The existing entry proposes Waiting for God; the line is at least as commonly placed in Gravity and Grace.
rows.unresolved: WORK AND TRANSLATOR TOGETHER. This is not a trivial edition choice: the work determines the source object and the translator determines the English expression. Keep genuinely open.

rows.source: Miles Davis, 'the note you play afterwards'
rows.evidence: UNVERIFIED, no primary source; kept at 4I on the manuscript's own hedge, 'is quoted as saying'.
rows.note: The manuscript deliberately preserves attribution uncertainty. Inventing a bibliography object would contradict that honesty - a bibliography entry would assert a source the book explicitly declines to claim.

rows.source: Socrates via Plato, 'The unexamined life is not worth living'
rows.object: Plato. *Apology* 38a.
rows.decision: ADD - source identity settled, bibliographic specificity unresolved
rows.evidence: VERIFIED EXACT with the Stephanus reference. No Plato entry exists anywhere in the book.
rows.unresolved: TRANSLATOR RECOVERY. Apology 38a identifies the textual object; the printed English still needs its mediator identified. Same sequencing as Plutarch: printed English -> identify mediator -> cite mediator -> rights. No translator guessing merely because the Greek source is public domain.

rows.source: John O'Donohue, 'May the light of your soul guide you'
rows.object: O'Donohue, John. *Anam Cara: A Book of Celtic Wisdom.* Harper Perennial, 1997.
rows.evidence: VERIFIED EXACT; the register names the work and the line's position as the blessing's opening.
rows.hold: Hold 'The Four Elements' until reverse reconciliation confirms it has no other live relationship.

rows.source: Martha Nussbaum, 'Emotions are not just the fuel'
rows.object: Nussbaum, Martha. *Upheavals of Thought: The Intelligence of Emotions.* Cambridge University Press, 2001.
rows.evidence: Bibliography relationship sound and already CORRECT.
rows.note: Register records VERIFIED VARIANT rather than exact; the wording check is final-text QA, not a bibliography matter.

rows.source: C. G. Jung, 'The meeting of two personalities'
rows.object: Jung, C. G. *Modern Man in Search of a Soul.* Translated by W. S. Dell and Cary F. Baynes. Harcourt Brace, 1933.
rows.evidence: Register names the work, CW 16, and the translators - unnamed in the manuscript.
rows.note: THIRD AND FINAL JUNG OBJECT. Three objects, three different sources: MDR (Ch2), Letters Vol. 1 (Ch5), Modern Man (Ch6). Modern Man is claimed after all and stays. Both real Jung defects were the same thing twice - missing translators, not missing entries.
rows.hold: The Red Book is now provisionally orphaned - no surviving object claims it - pending the final reverse check.

rows.source: Peter Gabriel, 'I own my fear / So it doesn't own me'
rows.object: Gabriel, Peter. "Darkness." *Up.* Real World Records, 2002.
rows.evidence: Gabriel's official Bandcamp page for 'Darkness' prints the exact line and identifies the track as from Up (2002).
rows.hold: 'Signal to Noise' can go at reverse reconciliation if no later surviving object uses it - both surviving Gabriel objects are now mapped, to 'Growing Up' and 'Darkness'.

rows.source: Pema Chodron, 'Things falling apart'
rows.object: Chodron, Pema. *When Things Fall Apart: Heart Advice for Difficult Times.* Shambhala, 1997.
rows.evidence: VERIFIED EXACT; bibliography CORRECT.
rows.note: Textual witness worth preserving: the manuscript keeps "It's just like that.", which the circulated online form drops.

rows.source: Richard Boothby, 'Our task in life consists precisely in a form of letting go'
rows.relationship: quotation, speaker quoted inside a container work
rows.object: Pollan, Michael. *How to Change Your Mind.* Penguin Press, 2018.
rows.evidence: Pollan's surrounding text introduces Richard Boothby, describes how he converted his insight about letting go into an ethic, and then gives the passage. The manuscript byline named Pollan.
rows.manuscript_repair: APPLIED. Byline now reads 'Richard Boothby, quoted in Michael Pollan, How to Change Your Mind'.
rows.note: CORRECT BOOK DOES NOT IMPLY CORRECT SPEAKER - the nonfiction equivalent of the Polonius, Satan, Hotspur and Melchizedek cases. The quotation census could not see it: the attribution named a real author and a real work and the sentence is genuinely in that work. It surfaced only when the bibliography pass asked what exact object the source relationship points to. Pollan stays in the bibliography because that is where the manuscript obtains Boothby's words.
rows.rights: likely_protected_standard - carry to Stage 6 under the corrected object

rows.source: Leonard Cohen, 'There is a crack, a crack in everything'
rows.object: Cohen, Leonard. "Anthem." *The Future.* Columbia, 1992.
rows.evidence: Applied at 4C; the byline carries it. The existing entry cites a 1968 poetry volume for a song released twenty-four years later.

rows.source: Laozi, 'Nothing is softer or more flexible than water'
rows.object: Laozi. *Tao Te Ching* 78. - English mediator unresolved
rows.evidence: VERIFIED EXACT against the chapter; the rendering is unnamed. No Tao Te Ching entry exists - the only one was Mitchell's, dropped when its quotation left at Stage 3.
rows.unresolved: DO NOT ATTACH A TRANSLATOR BY RESEMBLANCE. The manuscript's wording does not cleanly match the named translations checked - Cleary reads 'more flexible and yielding', Waley and others differ materially. If the exact rendering cannot be identified, replace it deliberately with a named translation later. Source identity settled, English mediator unresolved.

rows.source: Thomas Fuller, 'We never know the worth of water till the well is dry'
rows.object: Fuller, Thomas. *Gnomologia: Adagies and Proverbs, Wise Sentences and Witty Sayings.* 1732.
rows.evidence: VERIFIED VARIANT; bibliography CORRECT.
rows.note: Apparatus note, not a change: Fuller COMPILED this proverb, he did not compose it - the same shape as Aesop and Laozi.

rows.source: 'Healer, heal thyself', adapted from Luke 4:23
rows.evidence: PARAPHRASE/ADAPTED and correctly self-labelled in the byline; KJV reads 'Physician, heal thyself'. The census's positive control on the book's labelling practice.

rows.source: Audre Lorde, 'Our feelings are our most genuine paths to knowledge'
rows.object: Lorde, Audre. "Interview with Claudia Tate." In *Sister Outsider: Essays and Speeches.* Crossing Press, 1984, p. 132.
rows.evidence: VERIFIED EXACT with page, from the Claudia Tate interview.
rows.note: Naming the interview is preferable - it is the actual textual location.

findings: WATER IS THE CONTROL CHAPTER. Chapter 6 carried four CORRECT bibliography relationships and one correctly self-labelled adaptation - a notably high concentration of sound source relationships before this audit began. The apparatus was not uniformly weak, and the final record should say so.
